jobs.title: SDE, Alexa For Shopping
jobs.description:
**Description**
What if you could talk to your Amazon Store? With Alexa+ on Echo Show, customers can now do exactly that. The full Amazon store is live on Echo Show 15 and 21 — a new way to shop at home that combines voice as a natural way to express needs with the product details, reviews, and videos customers rely on to make confident decisions.
  
  
This product started with an ambitious question and was built from scratch — no prior version to iterate on, no existing architecture to extend, no playbook to follow. The team pioneered novel challenges including rendering the full, always-current Amazon store natively on Echo Show in real time, building visual grounding from scratch so Alexa's responses stay anchored to what the customer sees on screen, and creating a conversational commerce paradigm that lets customers skip screens entirely with natural language.
  
  
We are seeking a Software Development Engineer to help build the next chapter of this experience — scaling what we've built, expanding to new surfaces and marketplaces, and pushing the boundaries of agentic, multimodal shopping. As an early-career engineer on this team, you'll design and build meaningful components alongside experienced engineers, own your work through design, implementation, testing, and livesite, and grow quickly in a high-ownership environment.
  
  
This is greenfield, 0→1 work at the intersection of Generative AI, multimodal experiences, and conversational commerce. You will have the freedom to experiment, learn, and invent on behalf of our customers, and you'll work for a strong leadership team that optimizes for your growth and pairs you with mentors who will guide your career.
  
  
Key job responsibilities
  
  
As a Software Development Engineer I on this team, you will:
  
  

* Design, build, test, and operate features that scale and extend the Amazon Store experience on Echo Show and Fire devices.
* Write high-quality, well-tested code and participate actively in code reviews, both giving and receiving thoughtful feedback.
* Contribute to systems that render the Amazon store in real time, keep it in sync, and support conversational, multimodal shopping flows.
* Help extend the experience to new surfaces and international marketplaces, working through ambiguity where there is no existing playbook.
* Own your components end-to-end through livesite operations — monitoring, on-call participation, and continuous improvement of reliability and performance.
* Collaborate with engineering, science, product, and design partners across Alexa Shopping, including teammates in Seattle across time zones.
* Contribute ideas to technical designs, ask good questions, and grow your scope and autonomy over time with support from senior engineers and mentors.

A day in the life
  
  
Here's what a typical day might look like. You'll spend meaningful time building — designing and implementing features that scale the Amazon Store experience on Echo Show and Fire devices, whether that's improving how the store renders in real time, sharpening visual grounding, or extending the experience to a new marketplace. You'll write code, review your teammates', and get thoughtful feedback on yours.
  
  
Days blend focused coding with a short standup, design conversations where your ideas are genuinely wanted, and pairing with a senior engineer or mentor when you're working through something ambiguous. Because this is 0→1 work, you'll often be making decisions without a playbook — and that's the fun part. You'll partner closely with engineering, science, product, and design colleagues across Alexa Shopping, many of them in Seattle, so some collaboration spans time zones.
  
  
Your internal stakeholders are the product, design, and partner engineering teams shaping the Alexa+ shopping experience; your end customers are shoppers at home talking to their Echo Show, expecting it to just work. The problems you'll tackle range from "how do we keep the store always in sync and fast on-device?" to "how do we make a conversational shopping flow feel effortless?" — meaty, customer-facing problems where what you build lands in people's living rooms.
  
  
**About The Team**
We're the team that taught the Amazon Store to talk back. We took an idea that didn't have a blueprint and shipped it to customers' living rooms — and now we're just getting to the fun part: making it bigger, faster, and available to shoppers around the world.
  
  
Our mission is simple to say and hard to do: make shopping on Alexa feel effortless and delightful, no matter where a customer is or which device they reach for. We sit right where voice, vision, and Generative AI meet retail at Amazon scale — which means the problems we solve genuinely haven't been solved before, and the person who cracks them is often the newest engineer with a fresh idea.
  
  
Culture-wise, we're builders who like ambiguity and dislike bureaucracy. We ship, we learn, we tell stories over chai, and we celebrate the wins (and the instructive failures). We hire smart people and give them room to run — you'll own real problems from day one, with experienced engineers and mentors in your corner, not looking over your shoulder. We take the work seriously and ourselves a little less so. If you like the idea of building something customers can literally talk to, you'll fit right in.
  
  
**Basic Qualifications**

* Experience contributing to the architecture and design (architecture, design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and current systems

**Preferred Qualifications**

jobs.description:
India is the world's second-largest producer of fruits and vegetables, and loses over a lakh crore rupees of it every year between the farm and the shelf. Fresh Platter exists to fix that – not with an app, but by running the supply chain ourselves and engineering every step of it. We are hiring software engineers to build the brains of that system.

**About Fresh Platter**

Fresh Platter is a technology-driven fresh-produce supply-chain company, founded in Bengaluru in 2022. Every day we source from farms, then ripen, grade, pack and deliver fresh produce, using technology and data to improve quality, ensure consistent supply, minimise wastage and bring predictability to pricing. Around 100 people run the chain end to end, and the business is profitable.

We are also building our own machines and systems, because the bottlenecks we find in our operations cannot be fixed with software alone. Our harvest-handling rig cut bruising from around 30% to around 3%. Systems for farm selection, field scanning, produce movement and a fully automated packhouse are in build and design, with IISc and partner engineering firms. Five patent applications are filed.

Everything is built in three layers: a physical layer that moves and conditions produce, a sensing layer that reads its state, and an intelligence layer that decides what happens next and learns from the result. The crop changes. The architecture stays.

**The role**

We are building a high-quality software engineering team to own the sensing and intelligence layers, and the applications that run the business around them. You will join an existing team under our Tech Manager, and you will be expected to raise its bar, not just fill a seat.

We build with a new generation of AI-assisted development tools, seriously and every day. A small, sharp team here ships what used to need a large one. We will train you from your first week. If you already use these tools, good. If you have never touched one, that is fine – what we need is the raw ability to learn fast, think clearly and get things done.

**What you will build**

**Machines and sensing**

•   

The software that configures and controls our machines – reading their sensors, turning that data into decisions, and sending the right instructions back.

•   

The data path from sensor to screen: collection, storage, monitoring and alerts.

•   

Prototype-to-production work with our mechanical engineers, IISc and partner teams, tested on real machines in a real packhouse.

**Products and applications**

•   

The applications that run the chain: farm sourcing and procurement, ripening, grading and packing, inventory, logistics, quality and farm-to-customer traceability.

•   

Dashboards and alerts so teams see problems as they happen, not in next month's report.

•   

Integrations with the systems we already run – accounting, projects, mail and messaging – so data is captured once and flows wherever it is needed.

**AI-driven automation**

•   

Automation of the repetitive work across procurement, accounts and operations – checking purchase orders and vendor bills against their supporting documents, reconciliations, reporting and follow-ups.

•   

AI agents that read documents, emails and system records, decide what to do and act on it, with a person approving where it matters.

**Engineering practice**

•   

Own what you ship after it goes live – monitoring, fixes and improvements.

•   

Work across the stack: front end, back end, APIs, databases, device communication and data pipelines.

•   

Write tests, review code, deploy safely and document what you build.

•   

If you join with experience, help set the team's engineering standards and mentor the engineers who join after you.

**Who we are looking for**

•   

B.E. or B.Tech in Computer Science, Information Technology, Electronics and Communication, Electronics and Telecommunication, Electrical and Electronics, or a closely related engineering stream.

•   

0 to 4 years of experience. Freshers with a strong academic record and engineers who have shipped production software are both welcome. Title and responsibility will match experience.

•   

Solid programming fundamentals and problem-solving skills in at least one language.

•   

A working understanding of databases, web applications and APIs, and the ability to debug code you did not write.

•   

Someone who learns fast, goes deep rather than skimming, works around obstacles and stays steady when priorities change – humble enough to be trained from scratch, confident enough to question what does not make sense.

•   

You do not need to be from a top-tier college.

**What to know before you apply**

This is an on-site role at our facility in Cheemasandra, Bengaluru East, six days a week, with no remote or hybrid option – the machines you will work on are here. The team is lean, problems rarely arrive with neat specifications, and the hours are long. This is not a comfortable job. It is the fastest way we know to become an exceptionally capable engineer.

**Why join us**

•   

Your code runs real machines and a real supply chain the moment it is ready – no release queues, no waiting months to see your work in use.

•   

Patented systems co-developed with IISc and engineering firms, not another CRUD app.

•   

Learn AI-assisted development in your first job, not your fifth.

•   

Real ownership from your first month, working close to a founder who spent 18+ years in software and data systems before building this company.

•   

Grow as fast as you can prove yourself. We hire on potential and promote on delivery.

**What success looks like**

•   

Within 3 months, you are shipping features to production on your own.

•   

Within 6 months, you own one or more of our products end to end.

•   

Within 12 months, you can take any problem in the business and build the software that solves it.

**Description**
Are you eager to shape the future of video entertainment, from movies and TV shows to live sports events? Do you enjoy tackling complex challenges within large-scale systems? If so, we invite you to help build the future of entertainment with us at Prime Video!
  
  
Since its launch in 2007, Prime Video has been transforming the traditional television and movie industry. With a rapidly expanding library of high-quality content and availability in over 240 countries and territories, Prime Video is now a key strategic priority for Amazon. We invest heavily in acquiring, producing, and programming a diverse range of TV shows, movies, and live events. Our exclusive titles include "The Lord of the Rings," "The Boys," "The Wheel of Time," and "The Marvelous Mrs. Maisel," among others. Beyond our extensive On-Demand catalog, Prime Video offers a wide selection of Linear Channels and Live Sports, featuring major events like Thursday Night Football, the English Premier League, NBA, MLB, ATP tennis, French Open, and the UEFA Champions League. If this sparks your interest, read on!
  
  
Key job responsibilities
  
  

* Design, develop, and maintain highly scalable systems that power Prime Video’s streaming services.
* Define the architecture for our software, utilizing a broad range of technologies, programming languages, and systems.
* Implement and operate APIs that manage billions of playback start requests, ensuring seamless, low-latency content delivery.
* Collaborate with cross-functional teams to influence the overall technical strategy and contribute to the team’s long-term roadmap.
* Communicate effectively across teams and stakeholders, ensuring alignment with technical goals and project timelines.
* Apply creative problem-solving skills to address complex challenges.
* Stay ahead of industry trends and new technologies, integrating them where appropriate. Fluency in GenAI based developer efficiency tools is a plus.
* Mentor and guide other engineers, contributing to the overall growth and success of the engineering team.

A day in the life
  
  
As a software engineer on the Prime Video team, my day starts with diving into hands-on coding and technical problem-solving. I’m not just writing code—I’m helping to shape the architecture of complex systems that millions of people rely on every day. One of the most rewarding aspects of my role is seeing my work come to life when friends and family use Prime Video to watch their favorite shows and live sports.
  
  
My primary focus is on designing and maintaining the APIs that power every title on Prime Video. This involves creating highly reliable and low-latency systems that ensure users can start streaming their content with just a click. The challenges are unique, especially when it comes to managing the sheer scale of requests we handle daily. To tackle these, I leverage AWS technologies like EC2, S3, DynamoDB, Kinesis, and CloudFront.
  
  
Collaboration is a significant aspect of my role. I collaborate with a cross-functional team to align our technical strategies and define our long-term roadmap. It’s exhilarating to influence decisions that will shape the future of Prime Video. Throughout the day, I alternate between deep focus on coding and brainstorming sessions with my teammates to tackle novel challenges.

jobs.description:
**Position Name:** Middleware Developer (C&C++) — ADAS

**Years of Experience:** 3- 7 years

**Location:** Bengaluru, Karnataka

#### 

#### **About Vayavya Labs**

Vayavya Labs builds embedded software and firmware for the semiconductor and automotive industries, with deep expertise in low-level device software, driver automation, and safety-critical systems. Our engineers work close to the metal — bringing up silicon, writing production firmware, and validating it to the standards demanded by modern and autonomous vehicles. We are expanding our middleware and platform-software capability to support the next generation of software-defined vehicles, where robust, well-architected middleware is what connects hardware to the applications that run on it.

#### 

#### **About the Role**

We are looking for a C/C++ Middleware Developer to design, implement, and maintain the middleware layer of a vehicle compute platform built for ADAS and autonomous driving. This is the layer where inter-process communication frameworks, service daemons, hardware abstraction interfaces, and system services come together to carry sensor data and control signals between low-level drivers and the autonomy software that depends on them. You will work within and contribute to the team’s in-house C++ middleware frameworks — not building from scratch in isolation, but extending, hardening, and optimizing a shared codebase that other engineers build on.

The role combines strong C++ systems programming with an understanding of how embedded software stacks are organized — from device drivers through middleware services to application interfaces. You will collaborate closely with firmware engineers, driver developers, perception and planning teams, and will be expected to write production-quality, testable, well-documented code that runs in resource-constrained, safety-adjacent environments. You should be comfortable working in a large, shared C++ codebase with established patterns, contributing clean code that other engineers review, extend, and rely on.

#### 

#### **What You’ll Do**

* Design and implement middleware components in C++ (C++14/17) that provide well-defined interfaces between platform services, device drivers, and application software.
* Develop and maintain inter-process communication (IPC) frameworks — D-Bus like services, shared-memory interfaces, zero-copy transports (e.g. Eclipse iceoryx), POSIX message queues, and Unix domain sockets — for reliable, low-latency communication between system daemons, sensor pipelines, and application software.
* Implement system services and background daemons on embedded Linux — managing lifecycle, configuration, logging, health monitoring, and error recovery.
* Write and integrate hardware abstraction layers (HALs) that expose sensor data, actuator controls, and peripheral status to higher-level software through clean, versioned APIs.
* Develop middleware for vehicle communication stacks — receiving and routing CAN, Ethernet, or serial data from the platform’s networking layer and exposing it to application consumers as structured service interfaces.
* Build and maintain configuration management, parameter storage, and runtime-tunable settings frameworks for embedded platforms.
* Work within and contribute to the team’s in-house C++ middleware frameworks — understanding the existing architecture, following established coding patterns and API conventions, and extending the framework with new modules as the platform evolves.
* Integrate third-party and silicon-vendor SDKs into the middleware stack — wrapping vendor libraries behind clean, testable C++ interfaces that isolate the rest of the platform from vendor-specific APIs and versioning.
* Develop middleware components for sensor data routing — receiving high-bandwidth data from camera, lidar, and radar interfaces and delivering it to perception and fusion consumers through well-defined, latency-aware service interfaces.
* Implement platform health monitoring and diagnostics services — collecting hardware status, software health metrics, and error conditions from across the middleware stack and exposing them for logging, alerting, and fleet-level telemetry.
* Profile and optimize middleware for CPU usage, memory footprint, latency, and thread safety using tools such as perf, Valgrind, strace, and GDB.
* Write unit tests (Google Test / Google Mock), integration tests, and system-level tests for middleware components, and integrate them into CI/CD pipelines.
* Collaborate with firmware engineers on bring-up and integration — understanding how middleware depends on driver and BSP behavior, and debugging issues that span the middleware-driver boundary.
* Participate in architecture and design reviews, contribute to coding standards, and maintain clear technical documentation for middleware APIs and service interfaces.

#### **What You’ll Bring**

* 3–7 years of hands-on C/C++ software development experience, with at least 2 years focused on middleware, platform services, or system-level software.
* Strong modern C++ skills (C++14 or later) — comfortable with RAII, smart pointers, move semantics, STL containers and algorithms, templates, and lambda expressions in production code.
* Solid understanding of Linux system programming — processes, threads (pthreads / std::thread), synchronization primitives (mutexes, condition variables, semaphores), signals, file descriptors, epoll/select, and the POSIX API.
* Experience designing and implementing IPC mechanisms — at least one of: D-Bus (sd-bus or GDBus), shared memory, POSIX message queues, Unix domain sockets, or named pipes — in a multi-process embedded or systems-software context.
* Working knowledge of the Linux build and packaging ecosystem — CMake (and ideally colcon for ROS 2 workspaces) for build, pkg-config for dependency management, and familiarity with cross-compilation toolchains for ARM targets.
* Comfortable with debugging and profiling tools — GDB, Valgri
